Renowned for his prowess in identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities, Hu is a master at 'pwning' challenges, a testament to his deep understanding and innovative approach to security.

46656.title: Security Researcher
46656.bio: Zhihui Lin received an MSc in Information Security from UCL and BSc in Computer Science from the University of Sheffield, UK, and is now an independent security researcher specialising in database and LLM security research. Notably, he has been recognised as a Million Dollar Hacker for his significant contributions to many vulnerability bounty campaigns.

45627.title: Associate Professor
45627.company: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
45627.bio: Shuai Wang is an associate professor with substantiation (tenure) at CSE, HKUST. Prior to that, he was an assistant professor at CSE, HKUST (2019-2024), and was a postdoctoral scholar in the AST lab at ETH Zurich (2018-2019). He received his Ph.D. from Penn State University, and B.S. from Peking University.

44483.title: Vulnerability Researcher @ Claroty Team82
44483.bio: Noam Moshe is a vulnerability researcher at Claroty Team82. Noam specializes in vulnerability research, web applications pentesting, malware analysis, network forensics and ICS/SCADA security. In addition, Noam presented in well-known Hacking conferences like Blackhat/Defcon, as well as won Master of Pwn at Pwn2Own Miami 2023.

47177.title: Vulnerability Researcher @ Claroty Team82
47177.bio: Tomer Goldschmidt is a vulnerability researcher at Claroty Team82. Tomer specializes in vulnerability research, Embedded research, network forensics and ICS/SCADA security

45075.title: Vulnerability Researcher
45075.bio: Junoh Lee is vulnerability researcher at Theori. He is interested in reverse engineering and find a new attack vector, mostly in major OS like Windows and Mac OS. Also, he is interested in exploit techniques, such as writing exploit codes for the latest vulnerabilities by researching ways to bypass the latest mitigations. He is also a CTF player and has played in various world competitions such as DEFCON and WCTF.

48944.title: Vulnerability Researcher
48944.bio: Gwangun Jung is a security researcher at Theori. His main research areas are operating systems, virtualization, red teaming. He is the Pwn2own Vancouver 2024 Virtualization category winner targeting VMware Workstation and received CVEs from Linux/VMware/etc.

46713.title: Head of Security Analytics
46713.bio: Eduardo is a seasoned, results-driven leader with extensive experience in the data science and artificial intelligence fields. As the Head of Security Analytics at ING, he leads the strategic direction and execution of high-quality analytics and data strategy. His expertise in AI, data science, and analytics has been honed through a series of progressive leadership roles, including serving as the AI Practice Leader for IBM Benelux and Principal Data Scientist for IBM Europe, where he played a key role in defining the AI strategy at the EU level and developing industry-aligned AI-powered solutions. He has a proven track record of delivering value through data-driven insights, with experience in building and validating AI models and consulting for clients at IBM, Mobiquity and Easytobook. His academic background includes a Ph.D. in Atmospheric Physics from Wageningen University, the Netherlands, and several well-cited papers in top-tier international scientific journals. He has received a number of honours and awards in the US, Europe, and Brazil. He is certified as a Distinguished Data Scientist by the OpenGroup, and as of 2022, he acts as a board member for the Data Scientist profession certification. In 2023, he became a visiting researcher at the Cybersecurity Lab of the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management at Delft University.

49191.title: Senior Security Data Scientist
49191.bio:
Roberto is a Senior Security Data Scientist at ING's CISO department, where he has been instrumental in advancing the Analytics efforts for IAM over the past two years. His role involves integrating Analytics and AI into IAM's operations, enhancing efficiency and effectiveness. Additionally, Roberto leads an educational program designed to make AI accessible and valuable to individuals from diverse backgrounds, fostering better collaboration and understanding.

Prior to working at ING, Roberto spent a year at MICompany, where he developed and delivered AI-focused training programs for large enterprises. These programs ranged from teaching data scientists how to communicate effectively with business stakeholders to educating business professionals on the fundamentals and benefits of AI, and advising C-level executives on AI strategy. Roberto's career in data science began with an eight-year period at IBM. During his time there, he worked on and led numerous projects across a variety of industries, including finance, healthcare, and retail. His responsibilities included developing and implementing AI models, and providing strategic insights to drive business decisions.

Outside of his professional endeavors, Roberto enjoys 3D printing and hiking. He often combines these interests by designing custom hiking gear, bringing the same enthusiasm and curiosity to his hobbies as he does to his work.

49193.title: Security Data Scientist
49193.bio: Ignjat is a current Cyber Security Masters student with a passion for cyber anonymity, threat intelligence, software architecture, and applied cryptography.

49188.title: Senior Security Data Scientist
49188.bio: Alessandro is a Senior Consultant and Data Scientist with multiple experiences in different industries. He is skilled in Consulting, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data, and Machine Learning. He has a business and information technology background within international university programs in Italy, China, Brazil, Netherlands, and South Korea.

49192.title: Security Data Scientist
49192.bio: Arlindo is a Cosmologist working as a Data Scientist and Intelligent Automation Engineer, passionate about creating, deploying and leveraging state-of-the-art AI, Machine Learning and advanced statistical techniques, to help unlock insights and business value from data.

33595.title: PhD
33595.company: University of Applied Sciences FH Campus Wien
33595.bio: Adrian Dabrowski wrote his PhD about large infrastructures including the identifying fake base stations ("IMSI Catchers"). Before his PhD, he was a founding member of two hackerspaces in Vienna, Austria, and on the board of one of them.

45985.title: Dipl-Ing.
45985.bio: Gabriel Gegenhuber is PhD candidate in Vienna, Austria. Gabriel is conducting research in the area of cellular and mobile networks. This includes Internet measurement technologies, traffic classification systems (e.g., deep packet inspection), and technical measures that are used to detect net neutrality and privacy violations.

49861.title: Cybersecurity and Data Science Researcher (M.Sc. student)
49861.bio: Amit Finkman is an M.Sc. student in Software and Information Systems Engineering Department at Ben-Gurion University (BGU) and a researcher at the Telekom Innovation Labs at BGU specializing in Data Science and AI. Her research focuses on addressing privacy challenges in AI-driven code assistants, particularly mitigating code leakage in Large Language Models (LLMs). Her work contributes to safeguarding sensitive information in AI applications and advancing ethical AI development.

49891.title: Cybersecurity and AI Researcher (PhD student)
49891.bio: Avishag Shapira is a cybersecurity researcher with five years of experience. She holds a bachelor's and master's degree in Computer Science and is currently a Ph.D. student at Ben-Gurion University, where her research focuses on practical adversarial machine learning attacks and defenses.

49892.title: Cybersecurity and AI Researcher (M.Sc. student)
49892.bio: Eden Bar Kochva is an M.Sc. student in Software and Information Systems Engineering Department at Ben-Gurion University specializing in Cyber Security. Eden serves as a Cybersecurity and Data Science Researcher at CBG - Cyber Labs at Ben-Gurion University. Her research focuses on the privacy and security risks associated with large language model (LLM)-based code assistance tools.

42263.title: Professor, Vice Director
42263.company: Ben-Gurion University Cyber Security Research Center
42263.bio: Asaf Shabtai is the Vice Head of BGU Cyber Security Research Center, a Principal Investigator (PI) at the Telekom Innovation Labs at BGU, and a Professor in the Department of Software and Information Systems Engineering at BGU. His primary research interests are computer and network security, cyber security, web intelligence, machine learning and AI Security, security awareness and security of avionic and operational technology (OT) systems.

37528.title: Professor, Director
37528.company: Ben-Gurion University Cyber Security Research Center
37528.bio: Yuval Elovici is the director of the Telekom Innovation Laboratories at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (BGU), head of BGU Cyber Security Research Center, Professor in the Department of Software and Information Systems Engineering at BGU. His primary research interests are computer and network security, cyber security, web intelligence, information warfare, side channel attacks and AI Security.

49893.title: Engineering Lead
49893.bio: Inbar Maimon is an Engineering Lead at Cyber@Ben-Gurion University, with expertise in modern cloud infrastructure, container orchestration, and AI-driven applications. She has over three years of experience leading engineering teams and delivering scalable, real-world solutions. Inbar holds a B.Sc. in Software Engineering from Ben-Gurion University and is passionate about bridging academic research with practical applications to drive technological innovation.

49894.title: CTO
49894.company: Ben-Gurion University Cyber Security Research Center & Telekom Innovation Labs
49894.bio: Dudu Mimran is CTO at Telekom Innovation Labs Israel. Dudu is an inventor and tech leader with over 30 years of deep tech, startups and corporate innovation experience. In the recent 15 years he is leading advanced research in cyber security and machine learning for corporate customers. Strong background in startups, product and GTM strategy, and ideation.

43424.title: Staff Security Researcher
43424.bio: Stav Shulman is a Senior Cyber Security Researcher and Analyst for Google Cloud with significant expertise in reverse engineering and long-term tracking and hunting of state-sponsored actors. Stav started her career in Incident Response and analysis of mobile malware, focusing on the Android operating system. In the last few years, she has been tracking and analyzing different malware families and threat actors operating against Middle Eastern targets, as well as operations performed by Middle Eastern threat actors. In recent years, Stav presented her research at various conferences (including Kaspersky SAS, BlueHat, CyberWeek, ITDefense and BSidesTLV).

49202.title: PhD student in cryptography
49202.bio: Miro Haller is a PhD student at UC San Diego, advised by Nadia Heninger, working on applied cryptography and system security. He is using mathematical techniques for cryptanalysis and then leverages these attacks to identify the root causes of cryptography failures in practice, and build or improve systems to address these failures. Miro has published cryptographic attacks on MEGA—a provider of end-to-end encrypted cloud storage for over 300 million users—at IEEE Security and Privacy and Eurocrypt. These attacks would have enabled MEGA to recover any user's key material by tampering with only a handful of login attempts. After identifying the lack of a rigorous formal foundation for end-to-end encrypted cloud storage, Miro and his collaborators presented security notions and the first provably secure cloud storage scheme at CRYPTO'24. Moreover, Miro published multiple attacks at USENIX Security. He and his co-authors broke the RADIUS protocol, which is used for authentication and authorization in almost every router and VPN sold in the last twenty years. His other attacks are targeting Multi-Factor Key Derivation Functions (a USENIX'23 paper) and micro-architectural side-channel attacks on Intel SGX enclaves.

48298.title: Researcher
48298.bio: David is currently pursuing his PhD at TU Braunschweig, Germany. His research focus is on web security and automatically enforcing privacy and security guarantees in web applications. His work has been published at top academic venues (e.g., IEEE Security & Privacy, Usenix Security, or CCS), while he is also a frequent speaker at non academic venues such as RuhrSec or OWASP AppSec.

45132.title: Security Researcher
45132.bio: Zong Cao is a security researcher at Imperial Global Singapore. He has a keen interest in the exploration and exploitation of vulnerabilities across various types of software, with research targets including browsers, cloud virtualization, and operating systems. He has received multiple acknowledgments from manufacturers such as Microsoft, Apple, and Mozilla. Currently, he is exploring the potential applications of AI in these fields. His previous work has been presented at Black Hat Asia and Black Hat USA.

49233.title: Security Researcher
49233.bio: Qian Zhu is a graduate of the Institute of Information Engineering at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and a member of the Nese team. He specializes in web application security and cloud-native security, currently focusing on exploring attack surfaces in Cloud Service Models, and participates in cloud-based red team research.

49605.title: Security Engineer
49605.bio: Hongkun Chen is a security engineer who graduated from Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications. He specializes in Web security and endpoint security. Currently, he works at EagleCloud, where he is responsible for researching technologies related to Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR). He has been a speaker at conferences such as HITB and CanSecWest. He has also discovered critical vulnerabilities multiple times, earning acknowledgments from renowned companies like Oracle, IBM, and Apache

49174.title: Professor
49174.bio: Dr. Liu Yang is currently a full professor in Nanyang Technological University, director of the cybersecurity lab, and Executive Director of CyberSG R&D Programme Office (CRPO). In 2019, he received the University Leadership Forum Chair professorship at NTU, the President's Chair in 2024. Dr. Liu specializes in software engineering, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. His research has bridged the gap between the theory and practical usage of program analysis, data analysis and AI to evaluate the design and implementation of software for high assurance and security. Many of his research has been successfully commercialized. By now, he has more than 500 publications in top tier conferences and journals, and 25 best paper awards and one most influence system award in top software engineering conferences. He is also leading several major research centers including CRPO, Trustworthy AI in NTU (TAICeN) and CREATE center with ICL on medical device security. He has received a number of prestigious awards including MSRA Fellowship, TRF Fellowship, Nanyang Assistant Professor, Tan Chin Tuan Fellowship, Nanyang Research Award, ACM Distinguished Speaker, NRF Investigatorship and NTU Innovator (Entrepreneurship) Award.

49860.title: Security Engineer
49860.company: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences
49860.bio: Dr. Xiu Zhang is currently a security engineer at the Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Dr. Zhang focuses on Web security research, including vulnerability research of Cloud services and On-premises products, AI Agent research to assist penetration testing, and traffic-based cloud WAF security avoidance.

33062.title: Vice President of Defensive Services
33062.bio: Neil R. Wyler (a.k.a. Grifter) is the Vice President of Defensive Services for Coalfire. He has spent over 20 years as a security professional, focusing on penetration testing, physical security, incident response, and threat hunting. He has been a staff member of the Black Hat Security Briefings for 22 years and a member of the Senior Staff at DEF CON for 23 years. Neil has spoken at numerous security conferences worldwide, including Black Hat, DEF CON, and the RSA Conference. He has been the subject of various online, print, film, and television interviews, and has authored several books on information security. In his free time, Neil keeps himself busy as a member of both the DEF CON, and Black Hat CFP Review Boards, the Black Hat Training Review Board, the founder of DC801, and founder of his local hackerspace, 801 Labs.

33063.title: Managing Principal
33063.bio: Bart Stump is the Managing Principal at Coalfire, living in Salt Lake City, Utah. He has been working in security for over 17 years working for some of the top vendors and companies in the industry. He has been a Black Hat staff member for 14 years and was a goon at DEF CON for 11 years and is involved with many local security groups and meetups. Follow him on X/Twitter @theStump3r

45925.title: Security Researcher
45925.bio: R4nger is a security researcher at Cyber-Kunlun, his research focus on windows vulnerabilities hunting and exploitation.

40306.title: Student
40306.bio: Fangming Gu is a doctoral candidate at the Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences. His focus is on Windows security research and complex software reverse engineering. He also devotes time to build automated bug finding tools. You can follow Fangming on Twitter @afang5472.

33344.title: Sr. Manager Security Research
33344.bio: Jonathan Andersson is the manager of Trend Micro's Advanced Security Research Group under ZDI/Trend Micro Research since 2010. He has 33 years of professional experience in fields including software development, electronic design, FPGA & PCB design, reverse engineering, and information security. He currently specializes in hardware, firmware, and RF signal reverse engineering. He has presented his original research globally to top-tier infosec conferences as well as by invitation to CERN and DARPA. He holds 15 US patents and is the creator of the Capture the Signal contest, an RF blind signal analysis contest for hackers and radio enthusiasts.

49238.title: Vulnerability Researcher
49238.bio: Thanos Kaliyanakis has 27 years of hardware & PCB design, FPGA, and firmware development experience in the fields of communication and information security devices. He specializes in electrical design of analog and high-speed digital circuits for both embedded and server class designs with a current focus on automotive device reverse engineering and security research.

32054.title: Founder of Black Hat and DEF CON Conferences & Former Chief Security Officer and VP at ICANN
32054.company: U.S. Department of Homeland Security Advisory Council
32054.bio: Jeff Moss advises companies on security issues, both, electronic and physical, as well as speaking globally on the topic. He sits on several advisory boards helping enterprises make informed decisions on cyber risks. In April 2011 Mr. Moss was appointed as the Chief Security Officer for the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), a non-profit whose responsibilities include coordinating and ensuring the security, stability and resiliency of the Internet's unique global identifiers as well as maintaining the root zone of the Internet. This position involved managing the IT security of the ICANN networks and information systems, the physical security of ICANN facilities and meetings, and ensuring that ICANN meets its security and resiliency commitments to the multi stake holder community that oversees ICANN. This position involved extensive international travel and coordination with governments, law enforcement, and operational security communities in support of discussions around Internet Governance and security. Mr. Moss left this position at the end of 2013. Moss is the founder and creator of both Black Hat and DEF CON, two of the most influential information security conferences in the world, attracting over ten thousand people from around the world to learn the latest in security technology from those researchers who create it. Prior to creating Black Hat, Jeff was a director at Secure Computing Corporation where he helped establish their Professional Services Department in the United States, Asia, and Australia. His primary work was security assessments of large multi-national corporations. Jeff has also worked for Ernst & Young, LLP in their Information System Security division. Because of this unique background Jeff is uniquely qualified with his ability to bridge the gap between the underground researcher community and law enforcement, between the worlds of pure research and the responsible application of disclosure. Jeff is currently a member of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security Advisory Council (HSAC), providing advice and recommendations to the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security on matters related to homeland security. Jeff is a life member of the Council on Foreign Relations, which is an independent, nonpartisan membership organization, think tank, and publisher. In 2013, Jeff was appointed as a Nonresident Senior Fellow at the Atlantic Council, associated with the Cyber Statecraft Initiative, within the Brent Scowcroft Center on International Security. In 2014, Jeff joined the Georgetown University School of Law School Cybersecurity Advisory Committee. Jeff is also active in the World Economic Forum, and recently became a member of the Cyber Security Global Agenda Council for 2014-2016. In addition, Jeff earned the ICSA President's Award for Public Service in 2011.

34820.title: Professor, Dipartimento di Elettronica, Informazione e Bioingegneria
34820.bio: Stefano Zanero received a PhD in Computer Engineering from Politecnico di Milano, where he is currently a professor with the Dipartimento di Elettronica, Informazione e Bioingegneria. His research focuses on malware analysis, cyberphysical security, and cybersecurity in general. Besides teaching Computer Security and Digital Forensics and Cybercrime at Politecnico, he has an extensive speaking and training experience in Italy and abroad. He co-authored over 100 scientific papers and books. He is a Senior Member of the IEEE and of the Computer Society, which has named him a Distinguished Visitor and Distinguished Contributor; he is a lifetime senior member of the ACM, which has named him a Distinguished Speaker; and has been named a Fellow of the ISSA (Information System Security Association). Stefano also co-founded Secure Network, a leading cybersecurity assessment firm, and BankSealer, a startup in the FinTech sector that addresses fraud detection through machine learning techniques.

31738.title: Security Researcher
31738.bio: James Forshaw is a security researcher in Google's Project Zero. He has been involved with computer hardware and software security for over 10 years looking at a range of different platforms and applications. With a great interest in logical vulnerabilities, he's been listed as the #1 researcher for MSRC, as well as being a Pwn2Own and Microsoft Mitigation Bypass bounty winner. He has spoken at a number of security conferences including Black Hat USA, CanSecWest, Bluehat, HITB, and Infiltrate. He's also the author of two security books "Attacking Network Protocols" and Windows Security Internals, both available from NoStarch Press.

43053.title: Lead Hardware Security Engineer
43053.bio:
Meadow Ellis conducts hardware security research and engineering in the fintech world, she also specialises in out-of-bounds data exfiltration, physical security and surveillance technologies encompassing mechanical, electrical and software design. She has extensive experience in cooperating with law enforcement agencies, most recently with regards to financial crime. She lives and breathes in the blueteam camp. Recently she could have been seen with DEF CON 29, BSides Leeds, BSides Wales and BSides London where she also leads the Workshops team.
Meadow strives to approach information security from the people side trying to understand the reasons behind the failures, the human element that caused it and the changes needed to avoid it in the future - changes that need to start with us.

40340.title: Global Board of Directors
40340.bio:
Vandana Verma is a seasoned security professional. She is a seasoned speaker / Trainer and presented at various public events ranging from Global OWASP AppSec events to Black Hat events to regional events like BSides events in India.
She is part of the OWASP Global board of directors. She also works in various communities towards diversity initiatives InfosecGirls, WoSec and null. Vandana is a member of the Black Hat Asia and Europe Review Boards as well as multiple other conferences including Grace Hopper India, OWASP AppSec USA to name a few.
She has been the recipient of multiple prestigious awards like Cyber Security Leader of the Year Award 2023 by BSides, the Resilient CISO award by Dynamic CISO, Cyber Security Woman of the Year Award 2020 by Cyber Sec Awards, Application Security Influencer 2020 by Whitesource, Global cybersecurity influencer among IFSEC Global's Top Influencers in Security and Fire Category for 2019, Cybersecurity Women of the year award by Women Cyberjutsu Society in the Category Secure Coder. She has also been listed as one of the top women leaders in this field of technology and cybersecurity in India by Instasafe.
